rich_summary: This section recounts the aftermath of a secret plot by Duryodhana, Karna, Sakuni, and Duhsasana—approved by Dhritarashtra—to burn Kunti and the five Pandavas alive in the flammable house at Varanavata. Vidura, perceptive and loyal to the Pandavas, discerns the conspiracy and secretly arranges their escape by boat across the Ganges. The Pandavas flee into the forest while the lac house burns, killing the architect Purochana and an unfortunate Nishada woman with her children, leading the public to believe the Pandavas have died. Dhritarashtra and the Kuru court perform false mourning rites. The narrative then reveals Duryodhana’s deeper motive: jealousy of Bhima’s strength, Arjuna’s prowess, and especially the growing public support for Yudhishthira as rightful king, which threatens the Kauravas’ claim to the throne.

highlight_spans.why: Kanika’s counsel leaves Dhritarashtra troubled, setting the moral and political tension that leads to the conspiracy.
Vidura secretly warns Kunti and provides the boat, a pivotal act that saves the Pandavas and alters the course of the epic.
The tragic burning of the lac house and the deaths of the Nishada woman and her children create a grim emotional turning point.
Duryodhana’s speech to Dhritarashtra reveals the political fear driving the plot: the rising popularity and legitimacy of Yudhishthira.

top_scenes.scene_text: Vidura secretly advising Kunti at night by the riverside, pointing to a hidden boat waiting on the dark waters of the Ganges.
The blazing lac house collapsing in flames while townspeople watch in horror, believing the Pandavas have perished inside.
Duryodhana, tense and jealous, speaking urgently to the blind Dhritarashtra in a dim royal chamber about the rising popularity of Yudhishthira.
